policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word order only: 'full of the Holy Spirit' renders either sequence identically; ASV gives no cue to the Greek order.
ASV 'was led in the Spirit in the wilderness' renders the locative ev tei eremoi; the accusative eis ten eremon would give motion 'into the wilderness'.
ASV 'and when they were completed, he hungered' has no rendering of the added hysteron ('afterward').
ASV 'And the devil said unto him' is equally the rendering of eipen de and of kai eipen; ASV renders connective de as 'And' throughout.
ASV 'And Jesus answered unto him, It is written' has no 'saying'; the RP reading's legon would be rendered.
Presence or absence of the Greek article before anthropos is invisible in ASV 'Man shall not live by bread alone.'
ASV ends the quotation at 'by bread alone.' with no rendering of the added 'but by every word of God'.
ASV 'And he led him up, and showed him' names no subject 'the devil' and no 'into a high mountain'; the longer reading's two additions are both absent.
an and ean are orthographic variants of the same generalizing particle; 'to whomsoever I will' renders either.
ASV lacks any 'Get thee behind me, Satan', excluding r02; between the remaining two only the order of 'Jesus said unto him' differs, which English does not register.
Word order only: 'Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God' follows English syntax in either case.
ASV 'And he led him to Jerusalem' renders egagen de and kai egagen alike.

ASV 'and set him on the pinnacle' supplies the object English requires after 'set' whether or not auton stands in the Greek; the pronoun is not italicized as a supply but ASV does not italicize routine pronoun objects.
Recitative hoti introducing the quotation is untranslated in ASV either way.
English 'into the synagogue' requires the definite article regardless of whether ten stands in the Greek.
Word order only: 'the book of the prophet Isaiah' renders either sequence.

ASV 'he opened the book' fits anoixas directly and anaptyxas ('unrolled') equally, since the marginal 'Or, roll' shows the translators treated the object as a scroll; neither wording nor note distinguishes the verb.
ASV moves from 'to preach good tidings to the poor' straight to 'He hath sent me to proclaim release', with no 'to heal the brokenhearted'.
Word order only: 'the eyes of all in the synagogue' follows English syntax in either case.
All three differ only in the form of the negative, the article before huios, and word order; 'Is not this Joseph's son?' renders each.
ASV 'done at Capernaum' is neutral between eis and en, and ASV spells the name 'Capernaum' throughout regardless of the Greek spelling.
ASV 'there came a great famine over all the land' renders the preposition epi; the reading without it leaves an accusative of extent that ASV would not render 'over'.
ASV 'in the land of Sidon' renders the adjective Sidonias and the genitive Sidonos alike; the note concerns the spelling Sarepta only.

ASV 'many lepers in Israel in the time of Elisha the prophet' puts 'in Israel' before the Elisha phrase, against RP's order, but the two remaining readings are the same text differing only in how the shared words are displayed.
ASV 'that they might throw him down headlong' renders hoste with the infinitive and eis to with the infinitive alike; the first two readings differ only in punctuation.
ASV begins the speech at 'Ah! what have we to do with thee' with no 'saying'; the added legon would be rendered.
ASV 'he came out of him' carries the 'out' in the compound verb; ap' autou and ex autou are rendered alike.
English 'in the midst' requires the article regardless of whether to stands in the Greek.
ASV 'rose up from the synagogue' renders apo and ek alike.
hapantes and pantes are both rendered 'all'; ASV gives no cue to the strengthened form.
ASV 'he laid his hands on every one of them, and healed them' uses the simple past, which renders the imperfect etherapeuen and the aorist etherapeusen alike.
ASV 'crying out' renders kraugazonta and krazonta alike.
ASV reports the demons' words as 'Thou art the Son of God' with no 'the Christ'; the title appears only later in the narrator's clause 'they knew that he was the Christ'.
ASV 'to the other cities also' renders epi and eis alike.
ASV 'for therefore was I sent' renders the aorist apestalen; the perfect apestalmai would give 'have I been sent', which ASV renders so elsewhere.
ASV renders keryssein eis tas synagogas as 'preaching in the synagogues' (compare Mark 1:39), so 'in' does not distinguish eis from en.
ASV text reads 'the synagogues of Galilee' and relegates the other reading to the margin, 'Very many ancient authorities read Judaea.'
